items.title: Finite background groupoid and cocycle-weighted gauging data
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; conditional two-group prerequisite status and current readiness are recorded in the batch notes and Step-1 receipt.
items.statement:
Let $K$ be a finite ordered simplicial complex. A **finite background field groupoid** $\mathcal F(K)$ is a category whose objects are declared background fields and whose morphisms are the declared gauge equivalences, such that every morphism is invertible, there are finitely many isomorphism classes, and every automorphism group is finite. Distinct automorphisms are retained as distinct morphisms whenever the selected field model declares them distinct; their multiplicities determine the gauge-volume factor. Write $\pi_0(\mathcal F(K))$ for the isomorphism classes.

A **cocycle/action weight** on $\mathcal F(K)$ is a function $W_K:\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal F(K))\to U(1)$ such that $W_K(y)=W_K(x)$ for every morphism $x\to y$; this invariance is the degree-zero cocycle condition used here. Its normalized **gauging sum** is

$$ Z_K(W_K):=\sum_{[x]\in\pi_0(\mathcal F(K))} \frac{W_K(x)}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal F(K)}(x)|}. $$

The quotient notation in this sum means isomorphism classes, not a set quotient with automorphisms discarded. The sum is the integral of $W_K$ against finite groupoid cardinality.

For the proposed finite 2-group specialization, let $G$ be a finite group with identity $e$, let $A$ be a finite abelian group written additively, and let $\rho:G\to\operatorname{Aut}(A)$ be a left action. A normalized group 3-cocycle is a function $\beta:G^3\to A$ that vanishes if any argument is $e$ and satisfies

$$ \rho_g\beta(h,k,l)-\beta(gh,k,l)+\beta(g,hk,l)-\beta(g,h,kl)+\beta(g,h,k)=0. $$

A background on $K$ consists of a flat edge cochain $a_{ij}\in G$, with $a_{ij}a_{jk}=a_{ik}$ on each ordered triangle, and an $A$-valued 2-cochain $B_{ijk}$ based at vertex $i$ satisfying

$$ \rho_{a_{ij}}B_{jkl}-B_{ikl}+B_{ijl}-B_{ijk} =\beta(a_{ij},a_{jk},a_{kl}) $$

on every ordered tetrahedron; $\rho_{a_{ij}}$ transports a coefficient at vertex $j$ to vertex $i$. A vertex-and-edge gauge parameter consists of vertex labels $g_i\in G$ and edge labels $\lambda_{ij}\in A$ based at vertex $i$ and acts by

$$ a'_{ij}=g_i a_{ij}g_j^{-1}, $$

$$ \zeta_{ijk}=-\beta(g_i,a_{ij},a_{jk}) +\beta(a'_{ij},g_j,a_{jk})-\beta(a'_{ij},a'_{jk},g_k), $$

$$ B'_{ijk}=\rho_{g_i}B_{ijk}+\zeta_{ijk} +\rho_{a'_{ij}}\lambda_{jk}-\lambda_{ik}+\lambda_{ij}. $$

These equations specify candidate background objects and gauge maps. They define a particular finite background field groupoid only after the arrow convention, including its automorphism multiplicities, is specified and the gauge maps satisfy the consistency conditions in the hypotheses below. An action produced from a higher group cocycle is an admissible weight only after its invariance under those declared arrows has been established.

references.title: Gregory W. Moore and Vivek Saxena, TASI Lectures on Topological Field Theories and Differential Cohomology
references.locator: §§12–13, PDF pp. 50–53, for groupoids of finite gauge fields and the 1/|Aut| measure; §18, PDF pp. 65–66, for cocycle-weighted finite gauge actions; §§23.2–23.3, PDF pp. 92–99, for homotopy pullbacks and finite pushforward.

references.title: Daniel S. Freed and Frank Quinn, Chern-Simons Theory with Finite Gauge Group
references.locator: §2, PDF pp. 8–11, for the finite bundle groupoid, automorphism measure, and cocycle-weighted partition function.

references.title: Robbert Dijkgraaf and Edward Witten, Topological Gauge Theories and Group Cohomology
references.locator: §§6.2 and 6.4–6.5, PDF pp. 22–30, for the finite 3D cocycle action, ordered simplex weights, and gauge-invariance scope.

items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used; all field, arrow, and automorphism sets are finite.

items.title: Finite cocycle-weighted groupoid gauging and gluing
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; conditional two-group prerequisite status and current readiness are recorded in the batch notes and Step-1 receipt.
items.statement:
Let $K=K_1\cup_\Sigma K_2$ be a finite ordered simplicial complex written as a union of two finite subcomplexes with common subcomplex $\Sigma$. Let $\mathcal F$, $\mathcal F_1$, $\mathcal F_2$, and $\mathcal S$ be finite background field groupoids for $K$, $K_1$, $K_2$, and $\Sigma$, with restriction functors $r_i:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal S$. The homotopy pullback $\mathcal H=\mathcal F_2\times^h_{\mathcal S}\mathcal F_1$ has objects $(x_2,x_1,\alpha)$ with $\alpha:r_2(x_2)\overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow}r_1(x_1)$ and morphisms $(u_2,u_1)$ satisfying $r_1(u_1)\circ\alpha=\alpha'\circ r_2(u_2)$.

Assume that restriction induces an equivalence $J:\mathcal F\to\mathcal H$. Let $W,W_1,W_2$ be $U(1)$-valued cocycle/action weights on these groupoids, and assume that under $J$ the weight factors as $W(x_2,x_1,\alpha)=W_2(x_2)W_1(x_1)$. For each object $s$ of $\mathcal S$, define the homotopy fiber $(\mathcal F_i)_s$ to have objects $(x_i,\eta_i:r_i(x_i)\overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow}s)$ and morphisms $u_i$ satisfying $\eta'_i\circ r_i(u_i)=\eta_i$, and put

$$ Z_i(s):=\sum_{[(x_i,\eta_i)]\in\pi_0((\mathcal F_i)_s)} \frac{W_i(x_i)}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{(\mathcal F_i)_s}(x_i,\eta_i)|}. $$

Then the normalized gauging sums are finite, are invariant under replacement of a field by a gauge-isomorphic field, and satisfy

$$ Z_K(W)= \sum_{[s]\in\pi_0(\mathcal S)} \frac{Z_2(s)Z_1(s)}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal S}(s)|}. $$

This is a finite groupoid theorem. A finite cocycle action is covered only when its evaluated weights obey the stated arrow-invariance and gluing-factorization hypotheses.

references.title: Gregory W. Moore and Vivek Saxena, TASI Lectures on Topological Field Theories and Differential Cohomology
references.locator: §§23.2–23.3, PDF pp. 92–99, for homotopy-pullback correspondences, finite pushforward, and the requirement to use homotopy cardinality for gluing.

references.title: Daniel S. Freed and Frank Quinn, Chern-Simons Theory with Finite Gauge Group
references.locator: §2, PDF pp. 8–11, Lemma 2.4 and Theorem 2.13, for automorphism-weighted finite sums and the cocycle-weighted gluing law.

references.title: Robbert Dijkgraaf and Edward Witten, Topological Gauge Theories and Group Cohomology
references.locator: §§6.2 and 6.4–6.5, PDF pp. 22–30, for the finite 3D Dijkgraaf–Witten action and its ordered-triangulation conventions.

items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used; all groupoids, morphism sets, and sums are finite.

title: Finite Groupoid Gauging and Gluing — Examples

items.title: The normalized sum on a one-object finite groupoid
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; conditional two-group prerequisite status and current readiness are recorded in the batch notes and Step-1 receipt.
items.statement: Let $G=C_2=\{1,s\}$ with $s^2=1$. Let $BG$ be the category with one object $*$, with morphisms $\operatorname{Hom}(*,*)=G$ and composition given by multiplication in $G$. Give its unique object the weight $W(*)=1$. The normalized gauging sum of this finite background groupoid is $1/2$.

items.title: A nontrivial cocycle weight on the finite two-element gauge groupoid
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; conditional two-group prerequisite status and current readiness are recorded in the batch notes and Step-1 receipt.
items.statement: Let $G=C_2=\{1,s\}$ and let the finite background groupoid be the conjugation action groupoid $G//G$: its objects are $g\in G$, and an arrow labeled $h\in G$ sends $g$ to $hgh^{-1}$. Define the normalized group 1-cocycle $\chi:G\to U(1)$ by $\chi(1)=1$ and $\chi(s)=-1$, and set $W(g)=\chi(g)$. The action weight is invariant under every arrow, and the normalized gauging sum is zero.

items.title: The homotopy-pullback gluing factor for the two-element group
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; conditional two-group prerequisite status and current readiness are recorded in the batch notes and Step-1 receipt.
items.statement: Let $G=C_2=\{1,s\}$ and let both restriction functors be the identity functor on the one-object groupoid $BG$. Give both pieces and the glued groupoid the constant weight $1$, and define the glued groupoid to be the homotopy pullback $BG\times^h_{BG}BG$. Its normalized gauging sum is $1/2$. Each homotopy fiber of an identity restriction over the unique boundary object has normalized integral $1$, so the gluing formula gives the same value.
